_comment: How to find each shop look part's element in a client draft (lib/fill-part-look.mjs). A part is keyed by the framework database's css_element for the group's blocks (block_attributes.css_element), so the look table's rows and the older named settings are covered the same way. A locator names structure only: input type, ARIA role, autocomplete token, tag, position, repeated siblings, the kind of text an element holds (currency, count, words, none), what it holds and where it sits; the grammar is documented in lib/fill-part-look-page.mjs. Wording is never a signal. A part with no entry has no locator and shows in the report as such. `pages` roles are filled from the client's page map at run time (the file each WooCommerce page's draft lives in).

my-account-in._comment: The account's signed-in views (lib/part-look-signed-in.mjs): the draft is signed in on its sign-in page and read view by view; the client's my-account surface names the draft and the post.

shop-chips._comment: The shop's filter chips (F-6): WooCommerce's chips block, its look settings (sgsChip*, data rows seeded from src/blocks/extensions/extension-roster.json's filterLook and chipGap) read from the draft's row of pressable chips on the shop page. Every chips block of the shop template takes the one look.

shop-count._comment: The shop's results count: WooCommerce's results count block, its sgsCount* look settings read from the draft's line that counts the listing's cards (the first whole number in its text is the number of cards).

shop-sort._comment: The shop's sort select (F-6): WooCommerce's catalog sorting block, its sgsSort* look settings read from the draft's sort select on the shop page.

confirmation._comment: The order confirmation's order lines card (F-44): sgs/order-items' look read from the draft's lines and their totals row on the confirmation page the template-order-confirmation entry names (its draftIndex). Parts are keyed by the css_element of the block's rows; its thumbnail settings carry no css_element in the database, so they have no locator yet. The order page needs a real order to be seen, so the surface carries verify false: --verify reads, compares and writes it but opens no live page.

productcard._comment: photo: the card's picture link; title: the card's title words. Both anchor the parts below by where they sit (drawn over the photo, in the title's row), never by a class or a word.

tag._comment: The badge on the photo: a span holding words inside the picture link. A label drawn over the photo with no fill and no border is the brand wordmark (the brand part), and an amount or a percent over it is the saving badge.

brand._comment: The brand wordmark laid over the photo: words drawn over the picture with no fill of its own and no border (a scrim or nothing behind them) and no amount. A badge (a box) is the tag part; an amount or percent over the photo is the savingBadge part.

savingBadge._comment: A saving badge laid over the photo: an element holding an amount (Save £12, -£12) or a percent (20% off, -20%), over a card's picture.

wishlist._comment: The heart: a wordless round or square button holding a drawing (svg), drawn over the photo (its middle inside the photo's box, whether it sits in the photo's link or beside it), once per card.

swatch._comment: The colour dots: two or more wordless square buttons side by side that hold no picture (a photo strip's thumbnails hold one).

attributeTag._comment: The small tag beside the title: a box of its own (fill or border) with words and no amount, in the title's row, that is no link or button and not on the photo.

accountIn._comment: The account signed in, read view by view (lib/part-look-signed-in.mjs). A part with view "detail" is read only on an item's own page (opened from the first listed item); every other part on the tabs the account menu opens. Address cards are read only in a view that lists no amount (the orders and a subscription list amounts; an address card never does). The parts the signed-out group already reads (the fields, their labels, the page header) are not repeated here, so the two surfaces never write one setting twice.

orderCards._comment: An order card: a repeated card holding an amount and a control (its own open button), else a repeated control that itself holds an amount and an order's own sign, a date or a status pill (a whole-row button, as a one-file draft draws its orders); a saved list or a plan list of priced rows has neither.

detailHead._comment: The order page heading row: the first element holding a heading and no control (a view wrapper holding the back control is not it).

od-placed._comment: The line under the order page title: a line inside the heading row (beside the title), else the first words after the row.

shopchips._comment: A row of three or more pressable chips (buttons carrying aria-pressed, one pressed): the row is chip-list, a chip not pressed is chip, the pressed one chip-selected, and a count drawn inside a chip is chip-count. Parts are keyed by the css_element of the chips block's rows. chip-all is the first chip of the row when it is pressed on load (the unfiltered choice, proved by its count being larger than every other chip's: chip-all-count against chip-other-count); `probe: press` presses a chip that is not pressed on the open page (lib/part-look-press.mjs) and reads whether the pressed chip is released (one at a time: chip-single) or kept (chip-multiple).

shopcount._comment: The shop's results count: the smallest line of words, its own text, outside the cards and outside any control (a chip's own count is not it), whose first whole number is the number of cards on the page (the cards anchor is the product card group's). A line that counts anything else, or a page with no cards, is not it.

shopsort._comment: The shop's sort select: the first select on the shop page (a select inside a product card is the card's own choice, not the sort).

orderitems._comment: An order line is the smallest element holding a currency amount and two or more pieces of words of its own (the item's name and its options), not a control; a totals row is a row whose direct children are words then an amount. A line's name and options are its outermost pieces of words (the draft's runtime draws each value as a span inside the words around it, so a span inside another piece of words in the line is that piece's, not a line of its own). The card holding the lines is read only for the gap between rows (list); its padding is the card container's, not the block's.
